title: crescendo-shift-transfer-crib
content:
Purpose:
Quick transfer crib for the Crescendo shift (day -> night). Very terse — meant to be scanned in 2–3 minutes. Keep this page open during handoff.

Context: (short)
- Night shift covers hosted API + dedicated pools in us-west2 and eu-west1.
- High-sensitivity: model routing and fallback behavior has been flaky after the KV cache change on 2026-01-18.
- Current experiment: auto-fallback to smaller model-family when GPU queue latency > 250ms for 30s.

Top-of-shift quick checks (do these first, in order):
1) Pager/alerts: open SRE Oncall dashboard — note any active incidents.
   - If any active: read incident summary + timeline (Slack thread link in incident).
2) Redwood API health: curl -s -D - https://api.redwood.ai/health | head -n 20 
   - Expect 200 + JSON with uptime and version.
3) Model-serving queue length: kubectl -n inference get hpa/queue-metrics -o jsonpath='{.status.current}'; check > threshold 80%?
4) Redis/KV cache: redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 INFO memory | grep used_memory; if > 80% of maxmemory -> flush-lru candidate.
5) Dedicated pool utilization: dashboard -> Dedicated -> GPU Utilization; check us-west2 pool saturation.

Known flaky signals to watch:
- 'kv-cache-miss-spike' alert: often correlates with recent model rollouts. If miss rate > 30% sustained for 5m, consider routing to non-cached variant.
- 'latency-fanout' alert: token p95 > 700ms for api-generation route. Usual causes: long horizon batching, kernel fallback.
- 'routing-fallback-loop' (rare): repeated fallback between quantized and fp16 variants. Temporary fix: pin model variant via admin console for affected customer/route.

Immediate mitigation steps (order matters):
A) Throttling spike / queue backlog:
   - Reduce max-batch-size for model variant in the admin console to 8 (from 32) for the route showing highest latency.
   - Temporarily enable burst-capacity if on Dedicated (go-to: Dedicated -> Pool -> Enable burst).
B) KV cache exhaustion/misconfig:
   - Confirm redis memory pressure: redis-cli INFO -> used_memory_peak.
   - If urgent and eviction is happening, incrementally remove large keys: redis-cli --scan --pattern 'prefix:cache:*' | head -n 200 | xargs -n1 redis-cli DEL
   - Post-action: restart inference-worker pods one-by-one (drain + rollout) to refresh caches.
C) Model routing oscillation (fallback loop):
   - Pin the older model variant for the affected route (Console -> Models -> Route -> Pin) and notify ML infra.

Escalation/contact list (fast):
- SRE on-call (tier1): Pager ID: +1-555-0101 (use pager if not in Slack).
- ML Infra lead: Aisha Khan (slack @aisha; cell +1-555-0144) — for model pinning/rollback.
- Serving runtime eng: Marco Li (slack @marco; github PRs).
- Platform ops: ops@redwood.ai (use for Dedicated pool capacity toggles if console down).

Example quick commands (copy/paste)
- Check API health:
  curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .
- List inference pods and restart a specific node gracefully:
  kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference
  kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-worker --field-selector metadata.name=<pod>
- Redis memory via redis-cli:
  redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 INFO memory | egrep 'used_memory:|maxmemory:'

Temporary runbook edits (TODOs while on shift):
- Add a small script in /scripts/preflight that checks kv-cache hit-rate + queue length and outputs action hints (PR: infra/scripts#45). (ACTION: Marco)
- Add pinned-variant step to 'routing-fallback' incident playbook with exact console clicks (ACTION: Aisha)
- Update Dedicated pool runbook to include manual burst enable steps and billing notes (ACTION: me).

Open anomalies and notes to follow up:
- 2026-02-23 03:14UTC: brief p95 spike tied to a large customer rerun — confirm if that was a scheduled job (ticket JIRA-INV-7892 assigned to Eng Team Alpha).
- Observed repeated tiny OOMs in worker-7; log excerpt attached in incident thread. Suspect memory leak post-kernel-update.

Handoff summary for incoming shift (what I did / what I recommend):
- Did: nudged Dedicated us-west2 pool to enable 2 additional burst nodes, restarted inference-worker statefulset rolling (one pod at a time) to clear stale caches.
- Did: set temporary route pin for /v1/generate-default to model v2.3-quantized for customers A & B.
- Recommend: keep an eye on kv cache miss rate for next 30–60m. If misses persist, escalate to ML Infra for rollback of KV change (2026-01-18 patch).

Personal notes / brain dump (for later cleanup):
- Consider adding a small 'circuit-breaker' on routing decisions that requires 3 consecutive sampling intervals before falling back.
- Add metric that tags requests by 'was_cache_hit' for better debugging; currently we infer via logs which is slow.
- Could we add an automated message to customer console when we pin a model variant? reduces slack pings.

Rituals & small niceties for whoever's next:
- If you fix something big, leave one-line summary at top of this doc and put link to incident thread.
- If you touch Dedicated capacity settings, note billing impact in the incident comment.

Quick log snippets to search in Kibana (use time range around the alert):
- "kv_cache_miss_rate"
- "BatchScheduler::enqueue_delay"
- "fallback_to_variant"

End-of-shift TODO (incoming):
- Make sure any temporary pinning is either removed or documented as long-term change (tag: model-pin).
- Close any 'incident: triaged' tickets or add a follow-up owner.
- Copy this file into the incident channel summary if you started an incident.

Unresolved questions (add as you go):
- Did the 2026-01-18 KV patch include an eviction-policy tweak? I couldn't find it in the PR notes. (ask ML Infra)
- Is burst capacity charged per-minute or per-hour for Dedicated? I think per-minute but double-check with billing.

End — short signoff:
Jules (crescendo on-call) — shifting to handover. If I'm not around, ping Aisha (backup).
